verdict.rationale: PowerShell opened Explorer.exe with full access (0x1f3fff) via a call trace through .NET native images ending in UNKNOWN memory, then opened the newly spawned cmd.exe (child of Explorer, in c:\Users\Public) with 0x1fffff. This pattern matches PowerShell-driven process injection or parent-PID spoofing into Explorer to spawn a shell. The svchost events are routine service starts.
